name: Robin Ddu
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Robin Ddu (Robin Ddu ap Siencyn Bledrydd of Anglesey) was a Welsh poet who flourished about 1450. Around ninety of his poems survive in manuscript, many of them prophetic; he sided with the Tudors and made a pilgrimage to Rome in 1450.
The poem here is a fragment of an ode to Anglesey in George Borrow's English version, from Wild Wales, printed in Welsh Poems and Ballads (1915).

poems.title: Mon
poems.author: Robin Ddu
poems.note: From "Wild Wales". Printed as "From the Ode by Robin Ddu"; the source marks omissions with ellipses.
poems.translator: trans. George Borrow (Welsh Poems and Ballads, 1915)
poems.text:
Bread of the wholesomest is found
   In my mother-land of Anglesey;
Friendly bounteous men abound
   In Penmynnydd of Anglesey. . . .

Twelve sober men the muses woo,
   Twelve sober men in Anglesey,
Dwelling at home, like patriots true,
   In reverence for Anglesey. . .

Though Arvon graduate bards can boast,
Yet more canst thou, O Anglesey.
